featured_reviews.review_text: “Preeti Sandwich in Mulund West is a mixed bag. The food was genuinely great—fresh, tasty sandwiches that hit all the right spots. featured_reviews.name: Chetan Kasurde
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mahabaleshwar Juice Center, Mulund - A Must-Visit for Freshness!
​"If you're looking for the absolute best fresh fruit cream and juices in the Mulund/Thane area, look no further than Mahabaleshwar Juice Center. Their Strawberry Cream is the star attraction – it's incredibly fresh, perfectly sweet, and a real taste of Mahabaleshwar right here! The quality of their fruits, especially the seasonal ones like Strawberry, Alphonso Mango and Mulberry, is unmatched.
​I also highly recommend their thick milkshakes and juices—everything tastes genuinely fresh and authentic, not watered down or artificial. The service is quick, the staff is friendly, and the place has a great, energetic vibe.
​Don't skip: The iconic Strawberry Cream! It’s worth every rupee and every bite.
​An amazing spot for a refreshing, high-quality, and delicious treat. Five stars!"

featured_reviews.name: Bombay Bhukkad Gang
featured_reviews.review_text:
R-steam Hot near Paanch Rasta in Mulund offers a cozy dining experience with a limited number of tables, creating an intimate setting for guests. The ambience strikes a balance between not being too flashy or too understated. Each table comfortably accommodates four people, providing a generous seating arrangement. The R-steam is a pure veg restaurant.

We indulged in their specialty, the melted cheese garlic bread, which presented a delightful twist with its liquid cheese filling. Though our garlic bread was slightly overdone, the overall taste was delicious, especially when paired with the accompanying jar of green chutney, adding a satisfying hint of spiciness. The presentation was not that appealing as the plate was a bit messy with the butter or oil .

The highlight was their famous masala milk served in a charming glass bottle. While the price seemed a bit steep for the quantity, the drink impressed with an abundance of dry fruits and saffron, making it a mouthwatering treat. The cafe's late-night opening hours enhance its appeal, and our 1:15 AM visit left us with a yummy and pleasant experience, despite the slightly higher food prices. Guys do visit R-Steam Hot and let us know about your experience.

Average Rating :- 4.6⭐️

Hygiene               -4⭐️

featured_reviews.name: Isha
featured_reviews.review_text:
Very disappointing and concerning experience.

When I asked for regular drinking water, the staff refused and said I had to buy bottled water because they “don’t have a water connection due to construction work.” When I asked how they were preparing food without a water connection, they replied that they are using their Aquaguard but are “not sure about the quality of the water.” So it’s considered safe enough for cooking but not for drinking? That explanation made no sense and raised serious hygiene concerns. Restaurants are not allowed to deny water to customers.

There is no GST number printed on the bill. Assuming they aren't registered under GST. Which means they aren't paying indirect tax. Makes it very easy to evade direct taxes also.

Overall, very shady practices and poor service. I would strongly advise people to avoid this place.

featured_reviews.name: Karthik Iyer
featured_reviews.review_text:
"I traveled from very far specifically to visit Rekdee - Taste of the Streets in Mulund for their late night food. The experience was a masterclass in how inconsistent management and staff can drive away genuine customers.

The Logical Contradiction:
Upon arrival, the boy at the counter informed me that Misal Pav was not available, but Tari Pav was. When I questioned the logic—given that both dishes share the exact same Tari (curry) and Pav—he failed to provide a valid reason. He then claimed a specific '12 AM to 4 AM' rule where Misal Pav is simply not served. I initially accepted this as a business policy maybe thinking that tarri pav has more profit and it consumes less tari as compared to a misal so they can make around 4-5 tari pavs instead of making 1 misal for profit, choosing to be reasonable and patient.

The Blatant Bias:
The situation changed 10 minutes later when a different family arrived. It was clear the management was partial to this specific group. Suddenly, the '12 AM to 4 AM' rule vanished, and the same staff member announced he was taking 'last orders' for Misal Pav for them. When confronted, he shamelessly claimed the Misal had 'magically' come back into stock. Only after being caught in this lie did he dismissively say, 'If you want now, we can give you,' which entirely missed the point of my concern regarding fair treatment.

The Linguistic Insult & Cowardice:
When I advised the staff that rules should be consistent for everyone, the boy cowardly hid behind the owner, claiming he was just following orders—despite being the one who originally gave me the 'lecture.' To make matters worse, both the owner and the boy began speaking in Gujarati, assuming I wouldn't understand their comments about a 'mess being created.' They were visibly stunned when I informed them that I understood every word of their mockery.

The ‘Go Ahead and Write’ Dare:
When I told the staff that such an unprofessional experience deserved a public review, the boy arrogantly responded with, 'Yeah, go ahead and write.'
To the Owner: Here is the review your staff requested. It is disappointing to see an owner stand by while staff lies to customers and then joins them in mocking a guest in a different language. Petrol and time were wasted on a recommendation that clearly doesn't value its patrons
